question: The 'August Offer' of 1940 was made by which British government official?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Linlithgow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **‘August Offer’** was made by **Lord Linlithgow**, the then **Viceroy of India**, in **August 1940**.
 
• The offer was an attempt by the British government to secure Indian support during **World War II**.
 
• It promised to grant **Dominion Status** to India after the war.
 
• It also proposed to expand the **Executive Council of the Viceroy**, including more Indian members.
 
• The British government assured that a **Constituent Assembly** would be formed to frame the future Constitution of India, with provisions for minorities' consent.
 
• The **Indian National Congress** rejected the offer as it fell short of their demand for complete independence.
 
• The **Muslim League** found the offer insufficient and continued to press for the creation of **Pakistan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Neville Chamberlain**__

 __
 
• **Neville Chamberlain** was the **Prime Minister of the United Kingdom** from **1937 to 1940**.
 
• He is best known for his policy of **appeasement** towards Nazi Germany, particularly for signing the **Munich Agreement** in 1938.
 
• Chamberlain resigned in May 1940, succeeded by Winston Churchill.
 
 
 
• **Clement Attlee**__
 __
 
• **Clement Attlee** was the **Prime Minister of the United Kingdom** from **1945 to 1951**.
 
• He played a crucial role in granting **independence to India** in **1947**.
 
• His government also established the **National Health Service (NHS)** in the UK.
 
 
 
• **Winston Churchill**__
 
 
• **Winston Churchill** was the **Prime Minister of the United Kingdom** during **World War II**, serving from **1940 to 1945** and again from **1951 to 1955**.
 
• Churchill was known for his strong opposition to granting independence to India and referred to **Mahatma Gandhi** in derogatory terms.
 
• His leadership during the war earned him widespread recognition as a wartime leader.
